body:
In article <4lbdru$laa@villa.fc.net>, ricardo@paranoia.com (Ricardo Hector Gonzalez) writes:
|> kilgrtrt@loa.com (kilgrtrt) wrote:
|> > Let's not make the unabomber a hero.
|> 
|> But he is a hero.  He dared to say what most people are too afraid,

He is not a hero.  He is a terrorist.

|> oversocialized, or blind to say.  He confronted our social problems
|> with a thoughtful analysis which is rare in a time when media stupidity
|> is the main source of most people's "information" about the world
|> around them.  There are so few honest and intelligent people in today's
|> society so his Manifesto was incredibly refreshing.

It was overly long, boring and obviously the product of a confused, paranoid 
mind.

|> > He's a lazy coward
|> 
|> He's not lazy at all.  The work attributed to the UNABOM suspect is 
|> extremely well done and show great dedication to his task.  The FBI
|> profile shows that he is extremely intelligent and reads a broad range
|> of literature.  No doubt he has worked hard to develop his keen intellect.

He is intelligent, but he has wasted his intelligence.  The suspect, Ted K.,
has been unproductive for over 25 years.   His earnings have been very meager.
Ted K. has wasted his life living in the woods not doing useful, productive 
work.

|> He's not a coward.  He is one of the few that you can find today who
|> lives just as they believe is correct.  He discovered that society
|> was going insane and got away from it.  He discovered that the working
|> world is a lie so he moved away from it as much as possible.  He targeted
|> societal scumbags who trade the future of our grandchildren for their

Again, the people the unabomber were not 'scumbags' but productive citizens that
worked hard to earn a decent living.  What do have against people that work
for a living?


|> >scrawny little loser
|> 
|> So he's not a fat slob who spends his time eating more food than he needs?
|> He's a "loser" because he isn't enslaved in your concept of giving your
|> life to a corporation and then being a consumer on your "free time"?

Yes.  Ted K. appears to have been a filthy slob.

|> Maybe he just realizes how unnecessary these stupid societal values are
|> and chooses to do something much more meaningful with his life.
|> 
|> >with a twisted view of the world.
|> 
|> His view is "twisted" because it is different than yours?  Maybe you'd
|> do better if you had his 160-170 IQ and broad literary background to 
|> interpret the world.  You're just repeating what the media is telling
|> you to think, aren't you?  You shouldn't let them control your mind,
|> presuming that you still have one.

|> discuss them further?

Implementing his ideas would have disasterous for modern society.  

|> > Besides,anyone who has a positive view of the unabomber and expresses 
|> > it on a computer,is really missing the point.
|> 
|> Nope.  You're just a fool for not reading and understanding his Manifesto.
|> 
|>   202.  It would be hopeless for revolutionaries to try to attack the
|>         system without using SOME modern technology.  If nothing else
|>         they must use the communications media to spread their message.[...]
|> 
|> We're in alt.fan.unabomber to start the revolution and take back our freedom 
|> from the enslavers.

What a laugh.  We have the immense freedoms in the U.S.A. today because of the
hard work of generations of people working to build a better democracy.  Embracing the industrial revolution and the information revolution have furthered
the cause for liberty.

|> -Ric
|>
